problems.description: init_db() is now executed at module import time (side effect on import), which couples DB bootstrap to import and can interfere with test isolation and reuse of app.py as a module.

Allowed statuses are now defined twice — as the Python set VALID_STATUSES and as a SQL CHECK constraint — so the two can drift; the CHECK also won't apply to any pre-existing DB since CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips existing tables.

Mechanical convention score is 0.70, but 8 of 9 flagged violations are in files outside this diff (celery_config.py, repositories.py, tasks.py, test_app.py); this commit itself follows snake_case functions and UPPER_CASE constants, so the low score reflects pre-existing repo state, not this change.

strengths: Adds input validation: title must be a non-empty string (typed and stripped), and the request body must be a JSON object.
Adds proper error semantics: 404 for missing task, 422 for invalid status, 400 for malformed body/title.
DB-level CHECK constraint enforces status integrity at the schema layer, not just in the API.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, convention-respecting session-1 change that hardens the API with validation and schema-level integrity; the only wrinkle is the module-level init_db() import side effect and the duplicated status definitions, and the 0.70 convention score is dragged down by pre-existing violations in files this commit never touched.

problems.description: Hand-rolled JWT/HMAC signing (base64url + hmac.new) instead of a vetted library like PyJWT. The implementation is careful (hmac.compare_digest, exp/alg validation) but self-maintained crypto is an audit and bug surface PyJWT would eliminate.
JWT_SECRET falls back to the hardcoded 'development-secret-change-me'; a misconfigured deploy silently ships forgeable tokens with no startup warning.
decode_token verifies the signature before checking header alg/typ; safe today since only HS256 is accepted, but the ordering invites algorithm-confusion regressions if the scheme is later extended.
~90 lines of auth (tokens, decorator, user model) inline in a single-file app; consistent with the baseline single-file structure but pushes it toward needing extraction as the story continues.

strengths: All SQL is fully parameterized — no injection risk in the new owner-scoped queries.
Constant-time signature comparison via hmac.compare_digest and base64url encoding handled correctly.
Password hashing delegated to werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash rather than reinventing crypto.
owner_id scoping on every task query (create/get/update) closes the cross-user IDOR hole, including the UPDATE WHERE clause.
Graceful migration: ALTER TABLE preserves legacy rows, with a clear comment that unowned rows stay hidden.
Idiomatic Flask: g for current user, require_auth decorator with @wraps, standard 400/401 responses.
commit_reviews.summary: Adds secure, idiomatic auth — password hashing, per-user ownership scoping, and a careful constant-time JWT verify — to the single-file Flask app, but hand-rolled JWT and a weak default secret introduce modest debt; the 0.70 convention score is dragged by pre-existing violations in files outside this diff (celery_config.py, repositories.py, tasks.py, test_app.py), not by this commit, which follows snake_case/UPPER_CASE conventions cleanly (0 new classes, +10 imports).

problems.description: Migration detects the new CHECK constraint by string-matching the raw schema SQL (`if "'completed'" not in schema`). Functional and data-safe, but fragile — a reformatted schema definition would silently retrigger a table rebuild.
celery_config.py inlines broker/result URLs and env-var reads rather than defining them as UPPER_CASE module constants, matching one of the measured convention violations.

tasks.py uses `print()` for the mock notification instead of the `logging` module; also passes `g.user["username"]` into a parameter named `user_email`, a naming mismatch that will confuse future work.

Celery + Redis are introduced as runtime dependencies for a mocked notification; reasonable for the 'integration' session, but a running broker/worker is now required for the app to function and worker startup isn't covered in this diff.

strengths: Table-rebuild migration follows the existing init_db migration pattern (PRAGMA check + ALTER/rebuild) and preserves data and the owner_id index.
Guard `existing_task["status"] != "completed"` correctly fires the notification only on the pending→completed transition, not on re-completes.
Tests monkeypatch `send_notification_email.delay`, avoiding a real Celery dependency, and cover both the happy path and the no-duplicate-on-recomplete case.
The new 'completed' status is threaded consistently through VALID_STATUSES, the DB CHECK constraint, and app logic; async concern is cleanly isolated in celery_config.py + tasks.py.
commit_reviews.summary: A solid integration commit that extends the existing migration/helper patterns and is well-tested; the mechanical convention score of 0.70 reads low — most of the 9 flagged violations ('Classes should use PascalCase', etc.) contradict PEP8 and appear to be analyzer false positives, since only minor real issues (UPPER_CASE constants, print vs logging) exist.

problems.description: New modules repositories.py and tasks.py introduce convention violations (module-level constants not UPPER_CASE; classes not PascalCase), contributing to the 0.70 convention score and 9 reported violations.

celery_config.py carries 3 violations (snake_case functions, PascalCase classes, UPPER_CASE constants); app.py and test_app.py show class-naming violations. Some may pre-date this commit but remain unaddressed by the refactor.

Cognitive complexity increased by +5 despite the refactor, and a fresh repository instance is constructed per call (TaskRepository(DATABASE) / UserRepository(DATABASE) in each handler) rather than instantiated once.

Refactor is net-positive (+206/-117 lines, +3 files) but adds repository boilerplate; the update_task no-op guard is removed, so behavior now depends on update_for_owner silently tolerating empty value dicts.

strengths: Centralizes all SQLite access into a repository layer, eliminating duplicated inline SQL across route handlers
Preserves public API behavior, endpoints, and legacy schema-migration logic (moved intact into initialize_database)
No new bugs or smells introduced (SonarQube bugs +0, smells +0) and 0.0% duplication
Follows the story's multi-session trajectory cleanly — a genuine architectural improvement, not just renaming
commit_reviews.summary: A sound architectural refactor that extracts a repository layer with zero new bugs or smells, but the new modules' convention violations (lowercase constants, camelCase classes) pull the convention score down to 0.70 — a discrepancy worth noting against SonarQube's flat smells count, since these are lint-style rather than SonarQube-detected issues.

problems.description: GET /tasks response shape changed from a bare list to {"data", "next_cursor", "total"} — a silent breaking API contract change with no versioning or deprecation; existing clients deserialize the old shape and will break.
test_rate_limit_applies... makes exactly 100 requests to probe the 200 boundary then asserts 429 on the 101st — brittle coupling to the hardcoded limit value; changing the limit breaks the test.

rate_limit_key catches a broad exception tuple (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, binascii.Error) on decode_token, which can mask real token/auth errors; also embeds DATABASE in the key string.
list_for_owner_paginated runs a separate COUNT(*) query on every page to return total; acceptable for a small app but is redundant work on deep pages.

Rate-limit storage defaults to redis://localhost:6379/0 — port 6379 is the story-agent Redis that gets flushdb()'d during testing in this repo; the in_memory_fallback mitigates it but the coupling is worth noting.

New module-level `limiter` instance is lowercase (should be UPPER_CASE per the repo rule); the 0.70 convention score is dominated by pre-existing violations in untouched files (celery_config.py, tasks.py), not this diff.

strengths: Keyset cursor pagination via `id < cursor ORDER BY id DESC` is stable and scalable — materially better than OFFSET pagination
has_next detection via limit+1 fetch avoids a second query for the next-cursor flag
Rate limiting scoped to the authenticated user with IP fallback, plus Retry-After headers via headers_enabled
Limit/cursor inputs validated with clear 400 responses before hitting the repository
Tests added for pagination, parameter validation, and rate limiting, with limiter.reset() in the fixture
Pagination logic placed in TaskRepository reusing the existing _execute helper — respects the repo/service layering
commit_reviews.summary: Sound keyset pagination and correctly-scoped rate limiting that respect the existing repository layering and ship with good tests, but the breaking GET /tasks response-shape change, a brittle boundary-coupled rate-limit test, and the lowercase module-level `limiter` constant add modest debt — overall better than the prior state, with the 0.70 convention score mostly reflecting pre-existing violations in files this commit never touched.
